_meta.purpose: ADR-08 Phase 2 TARGET decision spec. The committed, human-readable golden mapping (input label/name -> resolved per-label script set -> UTS#39 restriction level -> severity -> action) that EVERY later phase (the Phase-4 analyzer, the Phase-5 matcher wiring) is graded against. There is NO existing-code oracle: today's feature blocks ALL IDN, the bluntness ADR-08 replaces. So this file AUTHORS the target, before any analyzer code exists.
_meta.rule: >=2 of the confusable_set co-occur in ONE label -> malicious; analysed PER-LABEL, never unioned across the dot; a name is malicious iff SOME label is.
_meta.scripts_property: Script_Extensions when present else Script; Common+Inherited dropped (transparent) -- see RESULTS/01 section 4.

restriction_levels.ascii_only: all code points are ASCII (UTS#39 ASCII-Only).
restriction_levels.single_script: after dropping Common/Inherited, the resolved set is a single script (UTS#39 Single Script).
restriction_levels.highly_restrictive: single script OR Latin + one of {Jpan: Han+Hiragana+Katakana, Kore: Han+Hangul, Hanb: Han+Bopomofo} (UTS#39 Highly Restrictive). The legit allow-set.
restriction_levels.non_restrictive: fails Highly Restrictive: any other multi-script mix (UTS#39 Moderately Restrictive / Minimally Restrictive / Unrestricted collapsed -- ADR-08 does not distinguish them, only 'fails Highly Restrictive').

severity_to_action.legit: none (resolve normally; never touched in Confusable mode).
severity_to_action.suspicious: alert (logged, resolution NOT broken) by default; block only when the opt-in suspicious->block sub-toggle is enabled.
severity_to_action.malicious: block by default (the block-malicious sub-toggle is default-ON; the operator may disable it, downgrading the action to alert).
severity_to_action.flagged: an undecodable / unresolvable-script label (malformed punycode, or a decoded label whose code points carry no letter-script). NOT malicious; surfaced as flagged so it is never silently passed and never crashes the resolver. Action under the default policy = alert (it is a non-legit anomaly, treated as the suspicious tier for the action mapping).

borderline_calls: Cherokee / Armenian / Coptic mixed with Latin are SUSPICIOUS, not malicious: they confuse with Latin but are outside the high-confidence {Latin,Cyrillic,Greek} trio and have legitimate single-script use; folding them into default-block risks FP without a measured TP need (RESULTS/01 section 3). Revisit only if a future corpus shows a real missed attack class.
Cyrillic+Greek (no Latin) IS malicious: the rule is >=2 of the trio, NOT Latin-anchored (RESULTS/01 section 3); proven by xn--mxa00ab.

An empty / control-char / emoji label resolves to NO letter-script -> severity 'flagged', NOT 'legit'. It carries no confusable mix so it is not malicious, but it is an anomaly and is surfaced (action = alert), never silently passed.
documented_limitations: Whole-script confusables (an all-Cyrillic look-alike of a Latin word, e.g. xn--80ak6aa92e 'аррӏе') are single-script -> NOT caught. Out of scope (ADR-08 section 7): catching them needs a confusables + protected-brand table, deliberately not built here.
Pure-ASCII typosquats (g00gle, rn-vs-m) are single-script ASCII, no xn-- -> NOT caught. Out of scope.

single_label.intent: A plain ASCII label is not an xn-- label at all -> the analyzer is never even invoked -> no-op. Pins the fast path.
Accented Latin (münchen) is single-script Latin -> legit.
All-Cyrillic (россия) is single-script -> legit even though Cyrillic is in the confusable trio (the rule needs >=2 of the trio).
All-Greek (ελλάδα) is single-script -> legit (mirror of the all-Cyrillic case).

Latin+CJK FP-guard: Han+Katakana (Japanese 'domain name') is UTS#39 Highly Restrictive -> legit. The single most important non-block case: a naive 'any multi-script -> block' would FALSE-POSITIVE here.

Latin+CJK FP-guard, full Japanese: ALL THREE scripts (Katakana メモ + Han 書 + Hiragana き) co-occur in ONE label -> UTS#39 Highly Restrictive -> legit. Real Japanese routinely mixes kanji + okurigana hiragana + katakana; this must NOT false-positive.
Latin+CJK FP-guard: Han+Hangul (Korean) is Highly Restrictive -> legit. Second CJK companion combo.
Latin+Cyrillic homograph (apple with Cyrillic а) -> >=2 of the trio -> malicious -> block by default.
Latin+Greek homograph (google with Greek ο) -> >=2 of the trio -> malicious -> block.
Cyrillic+Greek with NO Latin -> still >=2 of the trio -> malicious. Proves the rule is NOT Latin-anchored (borderline call, RESULTS/01).
Latin+Armenian: fails Highly Restrictive but Armenian is OUTSIDE the trio -> suspicious -> alert (block opt-in). Borderline call kept out of malicious.
Latin+Cherokee -> suspicious -> alert. Second non-trio confusable script.
Latin+Coptic -> suspicious -> alert. Third non-trio confusable script.

DOCUMENTED LIMITATION: an all-Cyrillic look-alike of 'apple' is single-script -> passes restriction-level analysis -> NOT caught. Asserted as a no-op to PIN that mixed-script detection does not catch whole-script confusables (ADR-08 section 7).

multi_label.name: example.рф
multi_label.intent: Latin SLD under Cyrillic .рф ccTLD. Each label is single-script -> legit. The WRONG whole-name union {Cyrillic,Latin} would falsely read malicious; per-label keeps it legit. Pins 'never union across the dot'.

multi_label.name: site.中国
multi_label.intent: Latin SLD under Han .中国 ccTLD -> per-label legit. Mirror of example.рф with a CJK TLD label.

multi_label.name: раypal.example.com
multi_label.intent: paypal homograph in the SUBDOMAIN label (раypal: Cyrillic mixed with Latin). Registry policy cannot validate subdomains; per-label analysis flags the offending label -> whole name malicious -> block.

edge_decode.note: empty punycode payload -> '' decodes ok, but an empty label resolves to NO scripts -> flagged (contentless; never asserted malicious or silently passed). Decode must NOT raise.
single overlong byte -> control char U+0080. Decodes ok but the char has no resolvable letter-script (resolves to the Unknown sentinel) -> flagged. NOT malicious, NOT silently legit.
incomplete punycode -> UnicodeDecodeError. MUST be caught and the label FLAGGED, never propagated (the resolver must not crash).
lone digit payload -> UnicodeDecodeError -> caught + flagged.
valid emoji label (pile of poo) -> decodes ok; emoji carries no letter-script (resolves to the Unknown sentinel) -> flagged. Not a confusable mix.
looks-ASCII payload decodes to junk Han ideographs -> single-script Han -> legit (decodes ok; no exception, no confusable mix).
